title: One-variable cutoff Cauchy transform with smooth parameters
statement:
Use the usual fields $\mathbf R$ and $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $c\in\mathbf C$, let $0<r<R$, and put $D_R=\{z\in\mathbf C:|z-c|<R\}$ and $D_r=\{z\in\mathbf C:|z-c|<r\}$. There exists a real-valued $C^\infty$ function $\chi$ on $\mathbf C$, equal to $1$ on a neighborhood of $\overline{D_r}$, whose support (the closure of its nonzero locus) is a compact subset of $D_R$, with the following properties. For every integer $m\geq0$, every open $P\subset\mathbf R^m$, and every smooth $h:D_R\times P\to\mathbf C$, set $H(\zeta,t)=\chi(\zeta)h(\zeta,t)$ on $D_R\times P$ and $H(\zeta,t)=0$ for $\zeta\notin D_R$. Then
$$ (T_\chi h)(z,t)=\frac1\pi\int_{\mathbf C}\frac{H(\zeta,t)}{z-\zeta}\,dA(\zeta) $$
is absolutely convergent and smooth on $\mathbf C\times P$, where $dA$ is planar Lebesgue measure and the integrand may be set to zero at $\zeta=z$. Here smooth means $C^\infty$ in all real coordinates. The map $T_\chi$ is complex-linear in $h$ and satisfies
$$\frac{\partial T_\chi h}{\partial\bar z}=\chi(z)h(z,t)\quad\hbox{on }D_R\times P,\qquad
\partial_t^\nu(T_\chi h)=T_\chi(\partial_t^\nu h)\quad\hbox{on }\mathbf C\times P$$
for every multi-index $\nu\in\mathbf N^m$, where $\partial/\partial\bar z=\tfrac12(\partial/\partial x+i\partial/\partial y)$ for $z=x+iy$. In particular $\partial T_\chi h/\partial\bar z=h$ on $D_r\times P$.

proof.text: Choose $r<a<b<R$ and apply the smooth ball-bump lemma on the underlying real inner product space $\mathbf C$, with radii $a,b$, to obtain $\chi$. It is one on $D_a$, an open neighborhood of $\overline{D_r}$, and its compact support is $\overline{D_b}\subset D_R$. These choices depend only on $c,r,R$.

source.place: I section 3.A, formula (3.2), Corollary (3.4), printed p.21, and I section 8, Exercise 8.5, printed p.61; read online, WANTED locally

proof.text: Form the stated zero extension $H$. It is smooth: on $D_R\times P$ this is the product of smooth functions; at every point outside $D_R$ it is identically zero on a neighborhood, since $\operatorname{supp}\chi\subset\overline{D_b}$ and $b<R$. It vanishes outside the single compact set $K=\overline{D_b}$ in the complex variable. Every real partial derivative of $H$ vanishes outside $K$ as well. Moreover $\partial_t^\nu H$ is the same zero extension formed from $\chi\partial_t^\nu h$, since $\chi$ is independent of $t$.

source.place: I section 3.A, formula (3.2), Corollary (3.4), printed p.21, and I section 8, Exercise 8.5, printed p.61; read online, WANTED locally

proof.text: By the Cauchy--Green test-function lemma, $k(w)=1/(\pi w)$, with $k(0)=0$, is locally integrable. Apply the parametric convolution lemma to $k,H,K,P$. This gives absolute convergence and joint real smoothness of $F(z,t)=\int k(w)H(z-w,t)\,dA(w)$. The substitution $\zeta=z-w$ preserves planar Lebesgue measure: its real linear part is $-I_2$, with absolute determinant one. Thus $F=T_\chi h$, including the chosen value zero at the singular point. The same substitution transports absolute convergence.

source.place: I section 3.A, formula (3.2), Corollary (3.4), printed p.21, and I section 8, Exercise 8.5, printed p.61; read online, WANTED locally

proof.text: For fixed $t$, use the total derivative formula of the convolution lemma in the real $z$ directions $1,i$ and take half the first plus $i/2$ times the second. After the same substitution this yields $\partial_{\bar z}T_\chi h=\int k(z-\zeta)\partial_{\bar\zeta}H(\zeta,t)\,dA(\zeta)$. The smooth function $u=H(-,t)$ has compact support, so the Cauchy--Green test-function identity makes the last expression $H(z,t)$. On $D_R\times P$ this is $\chi(z)h(z,t)$; on $D_r\times P$, $\chi=1$.

source.place: I section 3.A, formula (3.2), Corollary (3.4), printed p.21, and I section 8, Exercise 8.5, printed p.61; read online, WANTED locally

proof.text:
The parameter-direction part of the same derivative formula gives $\partial_{t_j}F=\int k(w)\partial_{t_j}H(z-w,t)\,dA(w)$. Iterate for $|
u|$ derivatives: the base $|
u|=0$ is the definition; at each induction step the differentiated $H$ is smooth with the same support $K$, so the convolution lemma applies again. Step 2 identifies the result with $T_\chi(\partial_t^
u h)$. Finally $H_{\alpha h+ eta h\prime}=\alpha H_h+ eta H_{h\prime}$ for $\alpha, eta\in\mathbf C$; linearity of the absolutely convergent integral proves complex linearity. For $m=0$ only the zero multi-index occurs, and the same proof applies.
